message.content:
The three most significant schisms in Christian history are:

| # | Schism | Approximate Year | Key Causes / Outcomes |
|---|--------|------------------|-----------------------|
| 1 | **Great Schism (East–West Schism)** | 1054 | Long‑standing theological, liturgical, and political differences between the Eastern (Byzantine) and Western (Roman) churches culminated in mutual excommunications. The split formalized the division into the Roman Catholic Church and the Eastern Orthodox Churches. |
| 2 | **Protestant Reformation** | 1517–1648 | Initiated by Martin Luther’s 95 Theses and later by other reformers (e.g., John Calvin, Huldrych Zwingli). It challenged papal authority, doctrinal abuses, and led to the creation of numerous Protestant denominations (Lutheran, Reformed, Anglican, etc.). |
| 3 | **East–West Schism (also called the Schism of 1054)** | 1054 | This is essentially the same event as the Great Schism listed above; it is often cited separately because it marks the definitive break between the Eastern Orthodox and Roman Catholic traditions. |

> **Note:** The “Great Schism” and the “East–West Schism” refer to the same historical event, so the list above reflects the common way these schisms are referenced in historical discussions.
